name: @app/consumer-ui
//: A shared UI package local to the consumer example, imported by name from the Cell's authored
source. It is workspace *source*, not a runtime module (#14): the compiler flattens this file
into the Cell artifact like any other source file, it never receives a dependency decision,
and it must never appear in `frontendLibraries`.
That is also why two Cells importing it would each carry their own copy: a React Context
declared here is local to each Cell, and module-scope state is per Cell. Cross-cell state is
Forguncy's (#4/#27), which is the boundary this example does not cross.
`react` is declared although it is decided `host`: a package that imports a module declares
it, and the bridge supplies the page's copy at compile time. Declaring it here is not an
instruction to bundle it — that is `fgc.lock.json`'s answer, not this manifest's.
`sideEffects: false` is what tells the bundler an unused export may be dropped, which is
the tree-shaking criterion #14 records. Nothing in this file does work at import time.
